Definition: from G3844 and G1510 (including its various forms); to be near, i.e. at hand; neuter present participle (singular) time being, or (plural) property:--come, X have, be here, + lack, (be here) present.
BiblicalUsage: Pareimi means to be near, to be present, to be at hand. Paul writes in 1 Corinthians 5:3 that though absent in body, he is present in spirit, and has already judged the man who did the deed. In 2 Corinthians 10:11 he warns that what he is in letters when absent, he will be in deed when present. Peter calls the truth in 2 Peter 1:12 the present truth, the truth that stands beside believers now and must be remembered.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe presence is a promise: Paul present in spirit, Peter present in truth, and Christ present with His people. That is why I hold that the truth is not far away, it is present, and I am to keep it near the way Peter kept reminding the church of it.
